summary: Autoscaler telemetry sampling gap leading to regional GPU thinness and degraded throughput
description:
Issue summary:
BrightDocs reported a midday sustained throughput degradation on their dedicated pool in us-east-1 starting ~2026-03-12 11:45 UTC. P50 remained acceptable but p95/p99 latencies spiked and overall token throughput dropped by ~35% for their pinned route. Impact: customer-facing search ranking pipelines had delayed responses; some requests timed out after 10s.

Impact:
- Persistent increased p95/p99 latency for dedicated route pinned to redwood/gpt-small-v1.
- Throughput drop ~35% on reserved pool for BrightDocs.
- Customer experiencing intermittent 503s and request timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in us-east-1.
- Route pinned to redwood/gpt-small-v1; fallback to open/gpt-neo-2.7b configured but observed fallback thrashing.

Initial observed behavior vs expected:
- Observed: autoscaler did not provision additional GPU capacity during a sustained increase in short-lived sidecar connections (sidecar logging/analytics) from several BrightDocs microservices. Telemetry sampling reported lower effective utilization for a 5-minute window, triggering autoscaler to undershoot.
- Expected: autoscaler should act on high-resolution signals and scale to maintain p95 SLOs; telemetry sampling should not mask bursty sidecar noise from customer-controlled processes.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer traffic pattern: many short-lived keepalive connections plus background sidecar log uploads (approx 200-400 small POSTs/sec) pinned to the same tenant during a 30-minute window.
Replayed in staging by running a mixed stream of 1000 short inference requests per minute combined with 250 sidecar metrics POSTs/sec to the tenant's sidecar endpoint.
Observe autoscaler telemetry dashboard and reserved pool slot allocation during the replay window.
Note: reproduce requires routing short sidecar connections to same pool to simulate noisy-neighbor effects.
logs: 2026-03-12T11:47:10Z - autoscaler: sample_window=300s util=0.42 signaled_scale=0 desired_replicas=2 actual_replicas=2
investigation_notes: 11:50 - Triage: Confirmed customer p95/p99 latency spikes correlate with sustained short-lived sidecar POST flood from the tenant. Sidecars opened many ephemeral connections that contributed to allocator attach churn and produced many small batches.

12:05 - Observed autoscaler sampling uses a 5-minute aggregated window and reduces signal weight for short bursts; config shows sampling_rate=0.1 and low-resolution aggregation in region us-east-1. This allowed the short-lived high-frequency events to be averaged down.

12:20 - Hypothesis: Telemetry sampling and aggregation smoothing caused the autoscaler to under-detect sustained but bursty attach pressure from the tenant. Autoscaler therefore did not grow the reserved pool quickly enough, causing GPU slot contention and prefetch/backpressure in the serving runtime.

12:35 - Cross-check: Other tenants in same pool with long-lived streams unaffected; problem localized to tenants with many short connections from sidecars. This matches noisy-neighbor pattern where many ephemeral streams cause slot fragmentation and throttle growth decisions.
12:55 - Noted fallback thrash: route fallback policies (pinned->fallback) caused extra attach churn when fallback variants were attempted, amplifying allocator pressure.

13:10 - Eng (SRE) requested a temporary override: force scale reserved-us-east for BrightDocs to +2 replicas and increase telemetry sampling resolution for that tenant for 10 minutes to validate effect.
timeline: 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - BrightDocs first reported p95 spike via support chat.
2026-03-12 11:50 UTC - Support created ticket and performed initial triage; collected logs and linked dashboards.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - SRE consulted; performed live metrics review and validated sampling gap hypothesis.
2026-03-12 12:20 UTC - Temporary scale override applied for tenant; observed immediate improvement in throughput and p99 latency reduced from 4.2s to 1.1s within 3 minutes.

2026-03-12 12:45 UTC - Scoped mitigation: increased telemetry resolution for tenant to sample_rate=1 for next 15 minutes; autoscaler reacted and maintained higher replica count during recovery window.
2026-03-12 13:30 UTC - Monitoring shows throughput recovering to expected levels; customer confirmed reduction in user-facing timeouts.
2026-03-14 09:00 UTC - Ongoing: engineering action item to adjust autoscaler sampling heuristics and add detection for sustained ephemeral-connection patterns.
comments: BrightDocs-SRE (via support chat) 2026-03-12T11:48: Customer sees search queries time out after 10s; this started suddenly at 11:44 UTC and only affects the pinned route.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12T11:53: Thanks — collecting traces and telemetry links. Can you share approximate qps and sidecar POST rate?

BrightDocs-Eng 2026-03-12T11:58: We're seeing ~80 qps normal inference plus ~300 sidecar metric POSTs/sec during our analytics window. Sidecars are configured to send small payloads on request completion.
SRE (Liam) 2026-03-12T12:06: We see attach churn and low aggregated util due to sampling resolution. Applying temporary scale override to validate. Will update in 5m.

SRE (Liam) 2026-03-12T12:23: After forcing +2 replicas for BrightDocs, p99 dropped to ~1.1s and throughput recovered. Reverting will prove reproducibility; holding override while we adjust telemetry for a test window.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12T12:40: Customer reports reduced timeouts and improved UX. We're keeping the ticket open for engineering follow-up to prevent recurrence.

Eng (Priya Menon) 2026-03-13T15:10: Proposed changes: add an ephemeral-connection detector metric (conn_duration_histogram + conn_rate_short) to weight the autoscaler signal and reduce sampling averaging for affected tenants. Linked GH PR for prototype.
SRE (Liam) 2026-03-14T08:45: Drafting rollout plan for autoscaler sampling config change in us-east; plan includes canary with a subset of reserved pools and telemetry guardrails.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: temporary forced scaling (+2 replicas) and transient increase in telemetry sampling resolution for tenant during incident window improved p99 latency and throughput. Root cause: autoscaler sampling and aggregation smoothed out bursty ephemeral-connection signals produced by customer-side sidecars, causing underscaling.

Planned fix: engineering will implement an 'ephemeral-connection' signal feature and change autoscaler sampling heuristics to detect sustained short-connection pressure. Rollout plan: canary in us-east reserved pools, monitoring thresholds, and automatic rollback on increased cost or instability. Expected ETA for code rollout: 2026-03-21.

Follow-ups assigned:
- ENG-3128: add conn_duration_histogram-based weight to autoscaler (assignee: Priya Menon).
- OPS-2140: improve per-tenant telemetry resolution overrides and alerting (assignee: Liam Zhao).
- CS-1209: provide BrightDocs with recommended sidecar batching guidance to reduce ephemeral connection frequency.
